Privacy Policy

opencode — a personal Google Workspace integration

Effective date: 15 November 2026 · Last updated: 15 November 2026

This policy describes how the opencode application (the "App") accesses, uses and stores Google user data. The App is a personal, single-operator tool: it is operated by, and used only by, Maksim Bureev ("I", "me"), the owner of maxxborer.com. It is not offered as a service to the public and has no other users.

1. What the App is

The App is a locally installed MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that connects an AI coding assistant running on my own computer to my own Google Workspace account. When I ask the assistant to do something with my mail, calendar or documents, the App calls the relevant Google API on my behalf, using an OAuth 2.0 token that I granted to my own account.

There is no hosted backend, no account system, no sign-up, and no multi-tenant data store. Every request is executed on my machine and sent directly to Google's APIs.

2. Google user data the App accesses

The App requests only the scopes needed for the features I use. All of them are granted to my own Google account by me, through Google's standard consent screen.

Google serviceScope grantedWhat the App can do with it
Gmailgmail.readonly, gmail.labels, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, gmail.sendSearch and read messages and threads, read attachments, create drafts, send mail, add or remove labels
Google Calendarcalendar, calendar.eventsList calendars and events, check availability, create, update and delete events
Google Drivedrive.readonly, drive.fileLocate and read files referenced by Google Docs, Sheets and Slides (Drive file management features are not used)
Google DocsdocumentsRead and edit document content
Google SheetsspreadsheetsRead and edit spreadsheet values and tables
Google SlidespresentationsRead and edit presentations
Google Taskstasks, tasks.readonlyRead and manage task lists and tasks
Google ContactscontactsSearch, read and create contacts
Google Formsforms.body, forms.responses.readonlyCreate forms, read form structure and responses
Basic identityopenid, userinfo.email, userinfo.profileIdentify which Google account a token belongs to

Google Drive management, Google Chat and Google Apps Script are explicitly not enabled.

3. How the data is used

Google user data is used for exactly one purpose: to carry out the action I requested in the assistant, at the moment I request it. For example, reading a message when I ask for a summary, or creating a calendar event when I ask for one.

  • No advertising, profiling, analytics or marketing use.
  • No selling, licensing or renting of data.
  • No automated decision-making about me that produces legal or similarly significant effects.
  • No use of Google user data to develop, improve or train generalized or foundation AI/ML models.

4. Storage and security

  • OAuth credentials (access and refresh tokens) are stored only on my own computer, in ~/.google_workspace_mcp/credentials/, in files readable by my user account only (permissions 600).
  • The OAuth client secret is stored on the same machine in ~/.config/opencode-secrets/ (600).
  • Content (message bodies, events, documents) is not persisted by the App. It is fetched on demand, held in memory for the duration of the request, and returned to the assistant session. Any file the App writes at my request is written to a local path I choose.
  • Data in transit uses HTTPS to Google's APIs. No Google user data is transmitted to any server other than Google's own APIs.

5. Sharing and disclosure

The App does not share, transfer or disclose Google user data to any third party. There are no sub-processors, no analytics providers, no cloud storage of Google user data, and no other people with access. The only recipient of the data is me, on my own machine.

Data may be disclosed only if I am legally required to do so, or to comply with a valid legal process — in practice the App has no mechanism to disclose data to anyone.

Limited Use disclosure. The App's use of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.

Specifically, Google user data is not transferred to others except as necessary to provide or improve the user-facing features described above, is not used for advertising, and is not read by humans — with the narrow exception of the account owner (me) reading his own data, and of automated security investigations where required by law.

6. Retention and deletion

The App keeps no copy of Google user data beyond the OAuth tokens. Tokens remain valid until revoked or until Google expires them.

To delete the stored data:

  • Revoke access: open myaccount.google.com/permissions, select the opencode app and choose "Delete all connections you have with opencode". Access stops immediately.
  • Delete local tokens: remove the files in ~/.google_workspace_mcp/credentials/. Without a refresh token the App can no longer reach the account.
  • Any exported file the App created at my request lives at the local path I specified and can be deleted like any other file.

Because there is no server-side storage, deletion of the local tokens and revocation of the grant are complete and irreversible: nothing remains to be erased elsewhere.

7. Your controls

Access is granted per Google account and can be limited or withdrawn at any time from the Google Account permissions page, or per scope on the consent screen. The App cannot re-acquire access without a new interactive consent by the account owner.

8. Children

The App is a personal developer tool and is not directed to, or used by, anyone under 18. It processes no data of minors.

9. This website

This site (maxxborer.com) is a static page. It sets no cookies, runs no analytics, embeds no third-party scripts and collects no personal data. Server-side logs are limited to what the hosting provider records for delivering the page.

10. Changes to this policy

If the App's data handling changes, this page will be updated and the "Last updated" date revised. Material changes will be reflected here before the corresponding change takes effect.
